subject: Re: FairShare corridor + true-up mechanics for per-token ladder
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@acmelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: FairShare corridor + true-up mechanics for per-token ladder

Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our call I attached an updated FairShare proposal that tries to balance Acme's desire for predictable unit economics with Redwood's need to avoid over-discounting during short-term spikes. High level:

- We propose a three-breakpoint per-token ladder (0-5B / 5B-20B / 20B+) with marginal discounts at each tier.
- Add a small "corridor" true-up (±10% on committed bands) that smooths billing surprises; Within the corridor customers get billed at expected marginals and any overage/underrun is true-upped at the quarter boundary.
- Introduce a soft-clawback for sustained underruns below 70% of commitment over two consecutive quarters (standard language, staged reductions rather than a lump clawback).

I've attached acme_fairshare_proposal_v2.pdf and a simple breakpoint math sheet so you can see unit rates side-by-side. Key asks for you: 1) are the corridors acceptable for procurement/legal, 2) any preference for marginal vs blended invoicing, and 3) whether Acme would be open to a six-month pilot at the proposed breakpoints before a full 12-month commit.

Thanks — happy to walk the numbers with Ben or Karthik if helpful.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@acmelabs.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmelabs.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: FairShare corridor + true-up mechanics for per-token ladder

Grace —

Appreciate the updated proposal and the math sheet. A few clarifying questions from procurement and finance: 

1) Marginal vs blended: Procurement prefers blended invoicing for month-to-month predictability (one effective per-token rate per invoice). Finance is worried blended obscures how the marginals affect long tail usage — do you offer an invoice appendix that shows the marginal math while billing a blended amount?

2) Corridor band: The ±10% corridor makes sense operationally, but can the corridor be asymmetric? For example, Acme would prefer a +15% overage allowance in Q1 of the deployment to account for onboarding spikes, with the -10% undershoot protection remaining the same.

3) Soft-clawback: the staged reductions sound reasonable, but legal needs language on the timing and cap (e.g., clawback capped at 20% of the annual commit in year one).

We can do a short call tomorrow to run through the numbers — do you have the Ben or Karthik on the line?

Thanks,
Emily Stanton
Head of Procurement, Acme Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@acmelabs.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 12:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FairShare corridor + true-up mechanics for per-token ladder

Emily —

We can absolutely produce a blended invoice for predictability and include a two-page appendix that line-items the marginal math (breakpoint quantities, per-tier per-token rates, and the resulting blended effective rate used for billing). That tends to satisfy both procurement and finance.

On the asymmetric corridor: operationally feasible. Proposed approach: allow a one-time asymmetric buffer for the first quarter only (+15% overage allowance) and then revert to symmetrical ±10% after Q1. We call it the onboarding buffer. If you prefer the asymmetric buffer to last longer, we can model the impact (it reduces the effective discount at the higher tiers).

Soft-clawback: agree with a cap. We recommend language: staged clawback applied only to the discount portion (not to usage), implemented over two quarters, capped at 20% of the annual committed discount in year one, reevaluated at renewal. I'll attach a worked example (see breakpoint_math_sheet.xlsx) that shows how a 20% cap flows through invoices and credits.

If you have time tomorrow at 10am ET, Karthik and I can join a call to run the scenarios.

- Ben
Lead Pricing Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@acmelabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FairShare corridor + true-up mechanics for per-token ladder

Emily — quick note on marginal vs blended and breakpoint selection:

- Marginal billing reflects true economics (you only pay the marginal rate for tokens in that band). Blended billing is simply an invoicing veneer; the underlying math is still marginal tiering. We typically surface both: marginals for internal cost/forecasting, blended for customer-facing invoices.

- Breakpoint sizing: the 5B / 20B breakpoints were chosen based on your historic 12-month run rate and projected ramp. If Acme is planning an initial pilot that materially reduces month 1-3 volumes, we can shift the lower breakpoint down (e.g., 3B) to reduce early effective unit price.

- Example scenario (from the sheet): under a 6-month pilot where actuals hit 60% of commit, the corridor + soft-clawback preserves ~85% of the committed discount for Redwood while giving Acme predictable downside protection.

Happy to run a sensitivity matrix live on the call.

Karthik
Sr. Revenue Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Stanton <emily.stanton@acmelabs.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:32:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: FairShare corridor + true-up mechanics for per-token ladder

Team —

Thanks — the appendix + blended invoice approach should work for procurement and finance. Procurement would like the asymmetric onboarding buffer (+15% for Q1) documented in the MSA and the clawback cap of 20% noted explicitly. For breakpoints: Acme will accept the 5B/20B structure for the 12-month commit, but we want an option at renewal to shift the lower breakpoint to 3B if the pilot under-indexes our projections.

Next steps: procurement will circulate a short amendment with the corridor and clawback bullets. Can you confirm you can deliver the appendix-generated sample invoice and the clause language by EOD Friday (I think that's 28 May for you)? If so, we'll proceed to DocuSign after internal approvals.

Also attaching the procurement checklist for Redwood to confirm legal wording and signatory names — I can upload the signed amendment once both sides confirm the exact clause language.

Best,
Emily Stanton
Head of Procurement, Acme Labs

Attachments: procurement_checklist.pdf
